angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 173,925 km at 111.03 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.0069 +/- 0.0627 mas (same row, RUWE 0.88): 111.03 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.25 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Adams et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of EPIC 206215704 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021PSJ.....2..152A/abstract): 173,925 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.407 +/- 0.095 solar masses from Heller et al. 2019, the stellar mass of EPIC 206215704 b's parameter set from Heller et al. 2019 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...627A..66H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3297 +/- 73 K from Adams et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of EPIC 206215704 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021PSJ.....2..152A/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Adams et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of EPIC 206215704 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021PSJ.....2..152A/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/epic-206215704.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.252, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
